findings.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:14 — FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym unconditionally with no nil-guard; if default_locale is ever nil/blank (e.g. during early boot/seed before the site setting is populated) this raises NoMethodError instead of degrading gracefully

- — I18n.locale is set immediately before I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! in set_locale, so the reported concern about stale I18n.locale does not materialize; FallbackLocaleList is stateless per-call (no shared mutable state) so it is thread-safe; @loaded_locales double-check in ensure_loaded! is redundant with the mutex-protected check in load_locale but not incorrect; removal of config.i18n.fallbacks=true is fully compensated by the new initializer's manual inclusion of I18n::Backend::Fallbacks and I18n.fallbacks assignment

config/initializers/i18n.rb:16 — FallbackLocaleList#[]` allocates a new 3-element array with `.uniq.compact` on every fallback lookup instead of memoizing per-locale, adding avoidable GC pressure on a hot path (every translation lookup that misses in the current locale).

app/controllers/application_controller.rb:158 — I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is now called unconditionally on every request, causing `self[I18n.locale].each { |l| I18n.ensure_loaded! l }` (array build + up to 3 membership checks) to run per-request even though after the first request for a given locale all fallback locales are already loaded, so this is redundant work repeated on every single request.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:62 — ensure_loaded!(locale)` checks `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` before calling `load_locale`, which redundantly re-checks the same membership again inside `load_locale`'s mutex, doubling the guard check per fallback locale per request; low-cost but easily avoided by calling `load_locale` directly.
- — load_locale` is properly guarded by `LOAD_MUTEX.synchronize` plus an `@loaded_locales.include?` double-check, so it is race-safe and does not repeat YAML/file I/O once a locale is loaded.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:21 — FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` calls `I18n.ensure_loaded! l`, but no such method exists on the top-level `I18n` module (the PR only adds `ensure_loaded!(locale)` as an instance method on `I18n::Backend::Simple` via lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb), so this raises `NoMethodError` every time it runs.

app/controllers/application_controller.rb:158 — I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is now called on every request from `set_locale`, so the NoMethodError bug in FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded! will break every single request rather than just an edge case.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:1 — The comment "order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb" refers to a file that does not exist anywhere in config/initializers (only i18n.rb is present), so there is no verifiable mechanism (naming, explicit require, or Rails initializer ordering hook) guaranteeing this file loads after freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb defines `ensure_loaded!` on `I18n::Backend::Simple`; if load order is ever violated this could NoMethodError at boot.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — FallbackLocaleList#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which requires a live DB connection; since `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` is installed globally at initializer time and used lazily on every translate/fallback lookup, any translate call during early boot, rake tasks, or asset precompilation without a DB connection will raise instead of degrading gracefully.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — No error handling wraps the `SiteSetting.default_locale` call in `FallbackLocaleList#[]`; if the DB is briefly unavailable during a request, the exception propagates up through I18n.translate with no fallback to a hardcoded default locale (e.g. :en), so a transient DB issue can break rendering of any page that requires translation instead of degrading gracefully.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:12 — FallbackLocaleList#[] (user locale, site locale, :en with .uniq/.compact ordering) has no unit test despite being new, non-trivial fallback logic; repo has no spec/ or test/ directory at all so this behavior is entirely unverified

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:62 — New ensure_loaded! method (guards against duplicate load_locale calls via @loaded_locales) ships with no test proving it actually prevents redundant loads or that it loads when not already present

goldens.comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:14 — FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym unconditionally with no nil-guard; if default_locale is ever nil/blank (e.g. during early boot/seed before the site setting is populated) this raises NoMethodError instead of degrading gracefully

adjudication.rationale: In config/initializers/i18n.rb, FallbackLocaleList#[] builds the fallback array as [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]. There is no nil/blank guard around SiteSetting.default_locale before calling .to_sym, so if it were ever nil this would raise NoMethodError. The diff doesn’t prove SiteSetting.default_locale can be nil at runtime (it may always be set), so this is a robustness/edge-case concern rather than a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - — I18n.locale is set immediately before I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! in set_locale, so the reported concern about stale I18n.locale does not materialize; FallbackLocaleList is stateless per-call (no shared mutable state) so it is thread-safe; @loaded_locales double-check in ensure_loaded! is redundant with the mutex-protected check in load_locale but not incorrect; removal of config.i18n.fallbacks=true is fully compensated by the new initializer's manual inclusion of I18n::Backend::Fallbacks and I18n.fallbacks assignment

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` after the locale-selection block in `set_locale`, and introduces an initializer that explicitly includes `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` and assigns `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`, while removing `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from environment configs—so the claimed concerns (stale `I18n.locale`, missing fallbacks after config removal, thread-unsafe shared mutable state in `FallbackLocaleList`) are not supported by what the diff shows. Some claims (e.g., redundancy vs a mutex inside `load_locale`) can’t be fully verified from the shown context, but nothing in the diff substantiates an actual issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:16 — FallbackLocaleList#[]` allocates a new 3-element array with `.uniq.compact` on every fallback lookup instead of memoizing per-locale, adding avoidable GC pressure on a hot path (every translation lookup that misses in the current locale).

adjudication.rationale: In config/initializers/i18n.rb, FallbackLocaleList#[] is implemented as `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`, which necessarily allocates a new Array and runs `uniq`/`compact` on each call. Since this method is used to compute fallbacks, it can be invoked frequently during fallback lookups, making the allocation/GC-pressure concern a concrete performance issue rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/application_controller.rb:158 — I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is now called unconditionally on every request, causing `self[I18n.locale].each { |l| I18n.ensure_loaded! l }` (array build + up to 3 membership checks) to run per-request even though after the first request for a given locale all fallback locales are already loaded, so this is redundant work repeated on every single request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` to `ApplicationController#set_locale`, which runs for every request. `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` (new in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`) rebuilds the fallback list (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`) and iterates it to call `I18n.ensure_loaded!` each time. Even though `I18n.ensure_loaded!(locale)` (added in `translate_accelerator.rb`) avoids re-loading already-loaded locales, the per-request array construction and iteration still occurs, making this a real, diff-grounded redundant-work/performance concern rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:62 — ensure_loaded!(locale)` checks `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` before calling `load_locale`, which redundantly re-checks the same membership again inside `load_locale`'s mutex, doubling the guard check per fallback locale per request; low-cost but easily avoided by calling `load_locale` directly.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ensure_loaded!(locale)` added with a guard `load_locale locale unless @loaded_locales.include?(locale)`, but it does not show `load_locale` performing the same `@loaded_locales.include?` check inside its mutex. Since that internal re-check is not present in the provided diff context, the claim of a redundant double-guard per call cannot be verified from the diff alone (and the issue described is a minor micro-optimization even if true).

adjudication_records.issue_text: - — load_locale` is properly guarded by `LOAD_MUTEX.synchronize` plus an `@loaded_locales.include?` double-check, so it is race-safe and does not repeat YAML/file I/O once a locale is loaded.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show `load_locale` being guarded by `LOAD_MUTEX.synchronize` or any “double-check” logic; only a new `ensure_loaded!(locale)` method is added, which checks `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` and then calls `load_locale`, but it does not show any mutex synchronization itself. Since the claimed race-safety and mutex-guarding cannot be verified from the provided diff (and the newly added path isn’t shown to be mutex-protected), the finding misreads/overstates what the diff demonstrates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — FallbackLocaleList#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which requires a live DB connection; since `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` is installed globally at initializer time and used lazily on every translate/fallback lookup, any translate call during early boot, rake tasks, or asset precompilation without a DB connection will raise instead of degrading gracefully.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly makes I18n fallbacks depend on `SiteSetting.default_locale` at runtime (`FallbackLocaleList#[]` returns `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`). Since `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` is set globally, any fallback evaluation will invoke `SiteSetting.default_locale`, creating a coupling between translation lookups and application settings availability. However, the claim that this *will* raise due to a missing DB connection cannot be verified from the diff alone (it depends on how `SiteSetting` is implemented), so it’s best treated as an architectural/boot-safety concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — No error handling wraps the `SiteSetting.default_locale` call in `FallbackLocaleList#[]`; if the DB is briefly unavailable during a request, the exception propagates up through I18n.translate with no fallback to a hardcoded default locale (e.g. :en), so a transient DB issue can break rendering of any page that requires translation instead of degrading gracefully.

adjudication.rationale: In `config/initializers/i18n.rb`, `FallbackLocaleList#[]` builds the fallback chain using `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym`. There is no rescue/guard around that call, so any exception (e.g., DB-backed `SiteSetting` raising) would prevent returning the array and could bubble up through I18n fallback resolution. While the diff doesn’t prove DB unavailability will occur or that translations should remain functional without DB, it does introduce a new runtime dependency on `SiteSetting.default_locale` in translation fallback computation without error handling, which is a concrete robustness/architecture concern grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:62 — New ensure_loaded! method (guards against duplicate load_locale calls via @loaded_locales) ships with no test proving it actually prevents redundant loads or that it loads when not already present

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `ensure_loaded!(locale)` method in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` that conditionally calls `load_locale` based on `@loaded_locales`, and the change is now exercised indirectly via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale`.
